insight: The file__apply_diff tool is under-utilized when file tools use the list-mount pattern. The LLM tends to mount 'write' and use it for all edits, never discovering apply_diff. Three nudging layers were added: (1) a prompt fragment naming apply_diff as preferred, (2) reordering list_tools output to show apply_diff before write, (3) enhanced descriptions marking apply_diff as preferred. The prompt fragment is the strongest lever since it's always present in the system prompt. If this is insufficient, the next step would be pre-mounting apply_diff, but that breaks the list-mount pattern's cleanliness.

file__apply_diff's format-aware fuzz can misapply hunks in two subtle ways: (1) an addition can land in the WRONG import block when the target and nearby blocks are structurally similar (adding `isBeaconConnected` to `./beacon-ws.js` instead landed inside the `drone-swarm-common` import), and (2) a multi-hunk edit on a region with back-to-back useEffect blocks can mangle the effects, merging two adjacent useEffects into one corrupted block. The import misapplication surfaces as a typecheck/build error; the useEffect mangling surfaces only as a failing test (the top-level render of a merged effect can still typecheck). Defense: after any multi-hunk apply_diff on a file with several similar import blocks or adjacent effects, re-read the targeted region AND run the authoritative `tsc -b`/`tsc --noEmit` plus the affected test file — do not rely on the LSP alone, since it can serve stale cached diagnostics that hide the true state.

Scripted test-mock sweeps and apply_diff both corrupt code in ways the src-only build cannot catch: (1) a node script that inserts a required registration member by anchoring on a tail field (`listMountedTools:`) mangles files where that field has a multi-line value (`listMountedTools: () =>\n  map(...)`) — the insert lands inside a SIBLING object or method body (compaction.test.ts got `emitEvent` inside the offer body; builtin-commands.test.ts inside a DroneSlashCommandContext ctx object), caught only by the vitest/esbuild transform failure, not tsc (which skips test/). (2) apply_diff's fuzz escapes `\n` as `\\n` inside patch string literals, so a written macro file had a literal backslash-n and its command never registered. Defenses: after any scripted/apply_diff sweep touching string literals or multi-line fields, grep the resulting file region and re-run the affected suite; trust the test runner over the LSP, which may serve stale cached diagnostics.
